subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw expose per-agent plugin installation before per-agent plugin discovery and activation security semantics are implemented?
rationale: The current branch creates a new install/config surface for plugin code placement, but existing runtime discovery still treats recorded plugin paths as global, so maintainer intent is needed before accepting any public scoped-install contract.

options.title: Pause for scoped lifecycle design
options.body: Require one coherent contract for scoped install, discovery, activation, update, uninstall, doctor, docs, and security policy before merging a user-facing flag.

options.title: Narrow to internal groundwork
options.body: Allow only non-user-facing storage refactoring if maintainers want incremental work, with no public `--agent` flag until runtime isolation is defined.

options.title: Close in favor of the canonical issue
options.body: Close this branch and keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97749 as the design and implementation tracker.

recommendation.title: Pause for scoped lifecycle design
recommendation.body: Require one coherent contract for scoped install, discovery, activation, update, uninstall, doctor, docs, and security policy before merging a user-facing flag.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin lifecycle work makes this the closest available code-history owner for the scoped install/update/uninstall contract.
